## What is mrpheus?

**mrpheus** is an R package for raw physiological signal analysis across
biological rhythms research. It ingests multi-modal physiological recordings —
polysomnography (EDF/EDF+), MRI-concurrent physiological logs (Philips PMU),
and EEG — and extracts features spanning three rhythm domains: **cardiac**
(QRS detection, HRV), **respiratory** (apnoea detection, respiratory metrics),
and **neural** (spindles, slow oscillations, automatic AASM sleep staging).

mrpheus is part of the [Circadia Lab](https://circadia-lab.uk) R ecosystem:

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **mrpheus** | Raw physiological signal analysis for biological rhythms research |
| [hypnor](https://github.com/circadia-bio/hypnor) | Hypnogram handling and sleep architecture metrics |
| [boldR](https://github.com/circadia-bio/boldR) | fMRIPrep BOLD derivatives → parcellated analysis |
| [zeitR](https://zeitr.circadia-lab.uk) | Wrist actigraphy analysis and circadian metrics |
| [syncR](https://github.com/circadia-bio/syncR) | Unified participant-indexed database |
| [slumbR](https://github.com/circadia-bio/slumbR) | Sleep diary processing |

---

## Installation

Install from [r-universe](https://circadia-bio.r-universe.dev) (recommended
— pre-built binaries, no compiler required):

```r
install.packages(
  "mrpheus",
  repos = c("https://circadia-bio.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)
```

Or install the development version directly from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("circadia-bio/mrpheus")
```

---

## PSG pipeline

The standard pipeline runs in seven steps. Each step produces a clean,
typed object that passes to the next function.

```r
library(mrpheus)

# 1. Read
rec <- read_edf("psg_001.edf")

# 2. Epoch and classify channels
psg <- prepare_psg(rec)

# 3. Preprocess
psg <- preprocess_psg(psg)

# 4. EOG correction
psg <- correct_eog_regression(psg)   # or correct_eog_ica()

# 5. Stage
stages <- stage_epochs(psg,
                       eeg_channel = "EEG Fpz-Cz",
                       eog_channel = "EOG horizontal",
                       emg_channel = "EMG chin")

# 6. Spectral analysis
bp  <- compute_band_power(psg, relative = TRUE)
tbp <- compute_temporal_bandpower(psg, hypno = stages$stage)

# 7. Export
hyp <- export_hypnogram(stages, start_time = rec$header$startTime,
                        participant_id = "sub-001")
attr(hyp, "sleep_architecture")
```

The sections below walk through each step in detail.

---

### 1. Reading a recording

`read_edf()` wraps `edfReader` with consistent output:

```r
rec <- read_edf("psg_001.edf")
rec
#> mrpheus EDF recording
#> i Path: psg_001.edf
#> i Duration: 7.98 hours
#> i Channels: 14
```

Pass `only_header = TRUE` to inspect the channel list without loading signal
data:

```r
hdr <- read_edf("psg_001.edf", only_header = TRUE)
```

---

### 2. Preparing a recording

`prepare_psg()` segments the recording into 30-second epochs, classifies
channels by type (EEG, EOG, EMG, ECG, RESP), and flags flat or bad channels:

```r
psg <- prepare_psg(rec)
psg
#> mrpheus PSG
#> i Epochs: 958 x 30 s
#> i Recording: 7.98 h
#> # A tibble: 14 x 4
#>   label              type  sample_rate   bad
#>   <chr>              <chr>       <dbl> <lgl>
#> 1 EEG Fpz-Cz         EEG           100 FALSE
#> 2 EOG horizontal      EOG           100 FALSE
#> ...
```

Channel classification uses regex patterns which can be overridden:

```r
psg <- prepare_psg(rec,
  eeg_pattern  = "EEG|C3|C4|F3|F4|O1|O2|Fpz|Pz",
  resp_pattern = "Thor|Abdo|Flow|SpO2|airflow"
)
```

---

### 3. Preprocessing

`preprocess_psg()` applies the standard EEG preprocessing pipeline to the
full continuous signal before re-epoching. The steps are:

| Step | Default |
|------|---------|
| Channel renaming | Optional — maps linked-ear names to 10-20 labels |
| DC removal | Subtracts per-channel mean |
| Powerline detection | Compares PSD at 50 and 60 Hz; picks the dominant one |
| Notch filter | 2nd-order Butterworth bandstop at powerline + harmonics |
| Bandpass filter | EEG 0.3–35 Hz · EOG 0.3–15 Hz · EMG 10–99 Hz · ECG 0.5–40 Hz |

```r
psg <- preprocess_psg(
  psg,
  channel_rename = c("C3-A2" = "C3", "C4-A1" = "C4")  # if needed
)
```

The individual filter functions (`remove_dc()`, `detect_powerline()`,
`notch_filter()`, `bandpass_filter()`) are also exported and work on any
plain numeric vector. See `vignette("eeg-preprocessing")` for details.

---

### 4. EOG artefact correction

Two methods are available. Both operate on the continuous signal and return a
cleaned `mrpheus_psg`.

**Regression** (fast, deterministic, works with a single EEG channel):

```r
psg <- correct_eog_regression(psg)
```

**ICA** (better for 4+ EEG channels, stochastic):

```r
psg <- correct_eog_ica(psg, n_components = 6L, threshold = 0.35)
```

See `vignette("eeg-preprocessing")` for guidance on which method to choose.

---

### 5. Automatic sleep staging

`stage_epochs()` stages each epoch using a pre-trained LightGBM model ported
from YASA (Vallat & Walker, 2021). Validated at 77.8 % epoch accuracy on the
Sleep-EDF Cassette dataset.

```r
stages <- stage_epochs(
  psg,
  eeg_channel = "EEG Fpz-Cz",
  eog_channel = "EOG horizontal",
  emg_channel = "EMG chin"
)
stages
#> # A tibble: 958 x 7
#>   epoch stage prob_W prob_N1 prob_N2 prob_N3 prob_REM
#>   <int> <int>  <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1     1     0  0.921   0.042   0.022   0.008    0.007
#> 2     2     0  0.874   0.081   0.031   0.007    0.007
#> 3     3     1  0.312   0.448   0.185   0.032    0.023
```

Stage codes follow the YASA/AASM convention: 0 = Wake, 1 = N1, 2 = N2,
3 = N3, 4 = REM, -1 = Artefact.

---

### 6. Spectral analysis

**Band power per epoch:**

```r
bp <- compute_band_power(psg, relative = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 958 x 9
#>   epoch channel    delta theta alpha sigma  beta gamma total_power
```

**Temporal band power across the night:**

```r
tbp <- compute_temporal_bandpower(psg, hypno = stages$stage)
#> # A tibble: 220 x 7
#>   time_hours epoch_start epoch_end dominant_stage band  power relative_power
```

See `vignette("spectral-analysis")` for visualisation examples.

**Sleep event detection:**

```r
sp <- compute_spindles(psg, channel = "EEG Fpz-Cz")
so <- compute_slow_oscillations(psg, channel = "EEG Fpz-Cz")
```

**Artefact detection:**

```r
art <- detect_artifacts(psg)
#> i Artefact epochs: 12 / 958 (1.3%)
```

---

### 7. Exporting the hypnogram

`export_hypnogram()` wraps the staging tibble in the `mrpheus_hypnogram` S3
class and pre-computes AASM sleep architecture metrics:

```r
hyp <- export_hypnogram(
  stages,
  epoch_s        = 30,
  start_time     = rec$header$startTime,
  participant_id = "sub-001"
)
hyp
#> -- mrpheus hypnogram --------
#> i Epochs:      958 x 30 s
#> i Participant: sub-001
#> i Source:      mrpheus / AASM
#> -- Sleep architecture -------
#>   TIB:  479 min  |  SPT:  461.5 min
#>   TST:  432.5 min  |  WASO: 29 min
#>   SE:   90.3 %    |  SME:  93.7 %
#>   SOL:  8.5 min   |  Lat_REM (AASM): 71.5 min
#>   N1:   6.1 %  |  N2:  52.4 %  |  N3: 18.2 %  |  REM: 23.3 %
```

Access the full metrics list:

```r
arch <- attr(hyp, "sleep_architecture")
arch$TST      # total sleep time (minutes)
arch$SE       # sleep efficiency (%)
arch$Lat_REM_AASM  # REM latency from sleep onset (AASM definition)
```

See `vignette("export-hypnogram")` for a full description of all metrics.

---

## MRI physiology pipeline

For recordings acquired alongside fMRI, mrpheus reads Philips PMU `.log`
files and runs Pan-Tompkins QRS detection:

```r
rec <- read_philips_physlog("sub-01_ses-01_physlog.log")
qrs <- detect_qrs(as.double(rec$C[, "v1raw"]), fs = rec$HDR$sfreq)
hr  <- compute_hr_signal(qrs)
```

See `vignette("mri-physiology")` for the full workflow including scan-window
alignment and RR-per-TR computation.
